frequency_question: How often do proposed or structurally enabled liquidity-absorption mandates successfully cross the barrier of internal institutional friction, legal pushback, and operational hurdles to reach official implementation within a tight window?
membership_rule: Includes any formal central bank announcement of a temporary or incremental reserve/liquidity ratio requirement designed to manage banking system liquidity. Excludes standard benchmark rate adjustments (repo/reverse repo changes) and permanent statutory reserve ratio changes executed during routine annual cycles.

cases.name: PBoC RRR targeted adjustments for liquidity management (Various 2010-2024)

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 4 named major instances of extraordinary reserve ratio tools deployed; institutional friction rarely stops implementation once drafted due to supreme regulatory fiat.
known_gaps: Minor technical postponements or internal draft modifications that were delayed beyond a specific quarter are not fully captured.
skeleton: Central bank regulatory interventions of an extraordinary liquidity-control nature implemented under existing broad statutory frameworks across major jurisdictions.
multiplier: 4 hits out of 4 documented major analogous structural interventions where the authority possessed direct legal mandate and operational machinery.
validity_reason: Central banking statutory powers and operational frameworks regarding reserve requirements remain stable across decades.
